citations.quote: Would activities that an RA 13 depositary performs in its capacity as a Transfer Agent (TA) (eg, processing payments in designated accounts) be subject to requirements under the CMR?
only when such LC is not acting as a Transfer Agent

That said, in the context of RA 13, handling of money which is not “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong will not be subject to the CMR. In such cases, the depositary is expected to observe relevant requirements under Schedule 11 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Schedule 11), in particular paragraphs 9 (relating to how subscription and redemption proceeds should be held) and 11 (relating to distribution proceeds).

concerns.question: transfer_agent does not specify a transaction, funds, capacity or evaluation time. It cannot distinguish the two readings in concurrent mixed-capacity cases without an additional scoped fact or an expressly clarified definition.

The vocabulary contains no Schedule 11 duty facts. Q1’s “In such cases” follows its non-scheme-money discussion; the text does not expressly extend that sentence to every Transfer Agent exclusion. Failure of this antecedent therefore establishes neither absence nor satisfaction of Schedule 11 duties.
The incorporated definitions and missing dependency are not supplied substantively. The scheme_money classification remains an external judgment, not a conclusion established by this Boolean.
Does “acting as a Transfer Agent” refer to the particular handling of money under examination, or to any concurrent Transfer Agent activity of the LC?
Does “only when” state merely a necessary condition, leaving other applicability requirements to incorporated legislation? The predicates here concern satisfaction of the selected antecedent only.

transfer_agent does not specify whether the role concerns these funds or unrelated activities. The first formalization assumes an entity-level evaluation; the second reading needs a relationship the fixed vocabulary does not expressly provide.
The vocabulary does not distinguish LC-held money from AE-held money or separately identify the AE’s capacity. The target expressly tests the role of “such LC”.

There is no input for Schedule 11 duties or their particular conditions. Q1’s “In such cases” follows its discussion of non-scheme money; continuing duties cannot be encoded as a universal consequence of a false Q1 predicate.
The incorporated definitions and missing dependency are unavailable in the supplied text. scheme_money and the other professionally judged classifications remain external inputs.
The vocabulary has no temporal indexing. Relevant-time evaluation must remain an explicit assumption; Q2’s timing discussion does not itself redefine the selected Q1 qualification.
Does “acting as a Transfer Agent” refer to the LC’s capacity in handling the particular money, or to any concurrent transfer-agent activity of that LC?

Does “only when” state merely a necessary condition, or does the surrounding “will apply” language make the listed conditions sufficient for this selected Q1 trigger? The predicates below concern antecedent satisfaction only.

Do Schedule 11 requirements extend to scheme money excluded solely by the transfer-agent qualification? Q1 expressly discusses non-scheme money; the supplied text does not expressly resolve this additional case.

transfer_agent has no explicit funds, transaction or time index. The entity-wide encoding is conditional on an interpretation assumption; the activity-specific alternative needs a relationship absent from the fixed vocabulary.
ra13_context aggregates LC and AE handling. It cannot separately represent the holder’s identity or the AE’s capacity, although the target expressly refers to the role of the LC.
No fact represents Schedule 11 requirements or their conditions. A false antecedent cannot encode either exemption from or compliance with those requirements.

The incorporated statutory definitions and identified missing dependency are not substantively available. scheme_money remains an external professional classification; Q2 and Q3 examples do not replace that definition.

The Boolean fragment tests antecedent satisfaction, not the legal modality connecting that antecedent to CMR applicability. Necessary-only and locally sufficient interpretations therefore cannot be distinguished by this expression alone.

No additional substantive parse of the exact target clause is sufficiently supported to add to the existing activity-specific and entity-wide alternatives. Does the intended restriction concern the particular money handling or any concurrent Transfer Agent activity?

Does “only when” express a necessary condition alone, or does “will apply” also supply sufficiency within the described Q1 circumstances? This modality disagreement does not change the selected antecedent predicate and cannot be resolved by treating its truth as a complete applicability verdict.

Do relevant Schedule 11 requirements cover scheme money excluded solely because of the Transfer Agent qualification? Q1’s “In such cases” immediately follows the non-scheme-money discussion, so a universal consequence for every failed antecedent is not established.
What evaluation time governs “acting”? Q2 addresses the start of a payment period and does not expressly establish the time for evaluating the Q1 role restriction.
